name: saw
description: Supply-chain worm hunting in your editor: the saw verdict for every folder you open, before you trust it.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Scanning works in Restricted Mode: saw only reads the folder. The settings that choose which program runs are read from your user settings only.

virtualWorkspaces.description: saw reads files from disk, so it needs a folder on this machine or on the remote it is connected to.

languageModelTools.name: saw_folderVerdict
languageModelTools.userDescription: Ask saw whether a workspace folder shows signs of a supply-chain worm before anything in it is installed or run.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns saw's supply-chain worm verdict (clean, residue, suspicious, not verified, or infected) for a workspace folder, with its strongest findings. Call it before you install dependencies (npm, pnpm, yarn, pip, poetry, cargo, go and the like), run scripts, tasks, tests or builds, or start a server in a folder, and again after pulling or checking out other code. If the verdict is infected, suspicious, not verified or unknown, do not do any of those things: stop, tell the user the verdict and findings, and ask how to continue. It is read-only: it never changes files and never runs anything from the folder. It may take up to a few minutes when the folder changed since the last scan.

folder.description: The workspace folder's name, or a path inside it (absolute, or relative to a workspace folder). Leave it out to get every open workspace folder.

viewsWelcome.contents:

saw.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `saw` program. Leave empty to find it on `PATH` or in `~/.local/bin`, or to use the one this extension installs.

saw.autoInstall.markdownDescription: Install saw with pipx when it is missing or too old, installing pipx first when the machine has none. Needs Python 3.11 or later and access to PyPI. Turn it off where software is installed only by an administrator.

saw.configPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to your own saw config (allowlist), passed as `saw scan -c`. A config inside the scanned folder is never used.

saw.scanOnStartup.description: Scan every workspace folder when the window opens, including folders you have not trusted yet.

saw.scanOnChange.markdownDescription: Scan a folder again when a file in it is saved, or when a file that can run code changes on disk (`.vscode/`, `package.json`, lockfiles, workflows).

saw.scanTimeoutSeconds.description: How long one scan of one folder may take before it is stopped and reported as incomplete.

scripts.package: pnpm run check-types && node esbuild.mjs --production && vsce package --no-dependencies --out saw.vsix
